title: Nethesis Insights
description: Every metric the five containers export: the four Go binaries and Traefik. Development stack only -- see deploy/dev/README.md.

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: Every target Prometheus is scraping. DOWN means the container is gone or its /metrics stopped answering -- not that the service is unhealthy, which its own health check reports.

panels.title: Time since last successful pass
panels.description: Each binary's periodic background pass. The series only exists once that pass has genuinely succeeded, so a missing tile after a restart is expected, not an alert.

panels.title: Process uptime
panels.description: A value that keeps resetting is a container in a restart loop.

panels.title: Requests per second, by service
panels.description: Every request each binary served, including its own /healthz and /metrics -- which is why an idle deployment is not at zero.

panels.title: Error responses per second, by status
panels.description: 4xx is usually a client without a credential; 5xx is the server's own fault. 503 on threatd's ingest path means the queue shed load.

panels.title: Request latency, p95
panels.description: Ingest is asynchronous on both queued pipelines, so this measures accepting a request, never the analysis behind it.

panels.title: Bundle queue
panels.description: Depth against the bound it is allowed to reach. The queue is in memory: depth at capacity means bundles are being refused, and a crash drops whatever is buffered.

panels.title: LLM calls per second, by outcome
panels.description: Attempts, not successes: the transient, permanent and parse paths all count here and all cost nothing. A transient error deliberately leaves the window claimable for the edge to retry.

panels.title: Model spend, running total
panels.description: Counted in micro-dollars by the server and divided here. Resets when the container restarts -- it is a process counter, not the stored ledger.

panels.title: Budget rejections per second, by reason
panels.description: Windows suppressed before the gate ran. Anything above zero means the spend ceiling or a per-system cap is now shaping what gets analysed.

panels.title: Ingest queue
panels.description: This queue bounds how many sanitized reports may wait on the single SQLite writer at once. It is not there to hide latency -- there is no LLM call on this path.

panels.title: Batches rejected per second (queue full)
panels.description: POST /v1/events answered 503 because the queue was saturated. The reporter is expected to retry; a batch lost here is not compensated, which is tolerable only because promotion needs three distinct systems.

panels.title: Cache results per second
panels.description: A miss is not a failure -- it is a credential the cache had not seen inside its TTL, and it becomes an upstream call.

panels.title: Upstream validator results per second
panels.description: What AUTH_VALIDATE_URL answered. 'unavailable' is the fail-closed path: authd answers 503 and every pipeline behind it rejects the request.

panels.title: Pass failures, last 24 h
panels.description: A failing consensus or cohort pass is silent otherwise: the blocklist feed keeps serving its previous snapshot rather than going blank.

panels.title: Pass runs per hour, by result
panels.description: Each binary runs exactly one periodic pass, on its own interval.

panels.title: Pass duration, p95
panels.description: A pass that grows towards its own interval is the first sign the fleet has outgrown a single instance -- none of these passes take a distributed lock.

panels.title: Requests per second, by response code
panels.description: Everything arriving on :443. A 401 here is the proxy doing its job: an unauthenticated request never reached a backend.

panels.title: Requests by routed backend, over the selected range
panels.description: Which router actually carried the traffic. One hue: the bars encode magnitude, and each one already names its own backend.

panels.title: TLS certificate
panels.description: Let's Encrypt renews at 30 days remaining. Amber here means a renewal has not happened when it should have.

panels.title: Proxy memory
panels.description: Traefik's own resident set. It is kept out of the per-service panels below so those stay within a colour set that a colourblind reader can separate.

panels.title: Open connections, by entrypoint
panels.description: The metrics entrypoint is loopback-only and normally shows the scrape in flight.

panels.title: Resident memory, by service
panels.description: Every pipeline holds its SQLite page cache here, so a flat line well above idle is normal.

panels.title: CPU used, by service
panels.description: Core-seconds per second: 1.0 is one core fully used.

panels.title: Goroutines, by service
panels.description: A count that climbs and never falls is a leak -- most often a response body or a row set that is not being closed.
